thread.title: U.S. stock futures mostly fall, hit by Facebook’s premarket dive

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: U.S. stock futures mostly fall, hit by Facebook’s premarket dive
text:
U.S. stock-index futures mostly pointed to a drop at the open Thursday, led lower by Facebook Inc.’s big premarket fall after its disappointing quarterly report.
What are the main benchmarks doing? S&P 500 futures ESU8, -0.20% lost 5.55 points, or 0.2%, to 2,835.75, while those for the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 NQU8, -0.84% shed 63.75 points, or 0.9%, to 7,405.75.
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average , YMU8, +0.13% , which doesn’t have Facebook as one of its components, bucked the negative trend, rising by 33 points, or 0.1%, to 25,436.
On Wednesday, the Dow DJIA, +0.68% , S&P 500 SPX, +0.91% and Nasdaq Composite COMP, +1.17% finished higher, rallying into the close after President Donald Trump and European Union chief Jean-Claude Juncker made a deal on trade .
The three gauges are showing year-to-date advances of 2.8% to 15%, as of Wednesday’s close.
What’s driving markets? Facebook FB, +1.32% has been among the tech giants powering the stock market’s gains this year, but the script just flipped. The social-media giant’s shares were dropping 19% in premarket action after the company late Wednesday revealed lower-than-expected quarterly revenue, slowing user growth and weak guidance .
Outside of Facebook-related gloom, European stocks on Thursday were cheering Wednesday’s upbeat meeting between Trump and the European Commission’s president. The two leaders reached a trade agreement that has been called short on specifics, but still significant. The deal shows the White House is willing to at least consider not letting global trade tensions spiral out of control, said a MarketWatch column .
What are strategists saying? “Facebook is expected to see its biggest one-day selloff when it opens later today. The big question will be whether it will bring down the rest of the FAANG stocks,” said Jasper Lawler, head of research at London Capital Group, in a note, referring to Facebook, Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.94% , Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +1.88% , Netflix Inc. NFLX, +1.55% and Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, +1.25% GOOGL, +1.41% .
“Whilst we expect Facebook’s results have a short-term impact on FAANG stocks, it’s more likely that we will start to see a de-coupling of Facebook from the group,” Lawler added.
Which other stocks are in focus? The companies on the earnings docket before the open include McDonald’s Corp. MCD, +0.60% , Mastercard Inc. MA, +2.19% , Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. BMY, +1.34% , Xerox Corp. XRX, -0.12% , Dunkin’ Brands Group Inc. DNKN, -0.37% , Allergan PLC AGN, +1.07% and American Airlines Group Inc. AAL, +1.98%
Which economic reports are on tap? Three reports are slated to hit at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, covering weekly jobless claims, durable goods orders and advance trade in goods. For those three releases, economists polled by MarketWatch expect 219,000 claims, June growth of 3.7% and a June deficit of $67.3 billion, respectively.

A second-quarter reading on housing vacancies is due to arrive at 10 a.m. Eastern.
What are other markets doing? European stocks SXXP, +0.40% traded higher after the U.S.-EU trade truce, while Asian markets finished mixed .
Gold futures GCQ8, -0.31% and oil futures CLU8, -0.04% were lower, as the ICE U.S. Dollar Index DXY, +0.07% also lost ground.
Victor Reklaitis Victor Reklaitis is a London-based markets writer for MarketWatch. Follow him on Twitter @VicRek .
